title: fix(service-datasource)!: the datasource admin API refuses to make a datasource managed while objects bind it with external
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu4rqxAsaQ9Xbbbf3naZ1vaL)_

Fixes #25277

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: narrowed

The datasource admin API (`POST /api/v1/datasources`, `PATCH /api/v1/datasources/NAME`) no longer stores a datasource that is managed while objects bind it with `external`. `createDatasource` and `updateDatasource` now judge the record they will persist against the objects bound to it, through the spec predicate `externalBindingDatasourceRefusal` (the one copy of the ADR-0015 §4.2 rule the metadata save door asks), before any secret or record write.

## The defect, measured on base `f0fdd45bb`

- The metadata save door refuses a datasource saved as `managed` (or with no `schemaMode`, the spec default) while objects bind it with `external` (`externalBindingSaveRefusal`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:22675`, datasource half `:22692`).
- `createDatasource` (`packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-admin-service.ts:608`) and `updateDatasource` (`:654`) write through `putDatasourceRecord` (`datasource-admin-plugin.ts:418`: `metadata.register` plus a direct `sys_metadata` insert/update). Neither enters `saveMetaItem`, so the pair the save door refuses was stored: on create (objects can name a datasource before it exists, and the save door gives no verdict on a binding whose datasource it cannot see) and on a `PATCH` that sets `schemaMode: 'managed'`.

## What changed

- `DatasourceAdminService` (`datasource-admin-service.ts`): a private `boundExternalRefusal(record)` asks the predicate once per object that names the datasource, and counts only its `managed` verdict, exactly as the save door's datasource half does. One line per bound object, each `schemaMode: ` plus the predicate's own message, under the door's `Invalid datasource 'NAME'.` heading. It is thrown as the door's other record refusals are, so the route answers `400 DATASOURCE_ADMIN_ERROR` (the code this service already uses; no new error code).
  - `createDatasource`: judged right after the existing record judgement, before `writeSecret` and `putDatasourceRecord`.
  - `updateDatasource`: the merged record, under the condition the record judgement already uses (a supplied secret or a patched `driver` / `schemaMode` / `config` / `external` / `pool`). A `label` / `active`-only write is not judged, so a row that already pairs badly can still be renamed or taken out of service.
- `DatasourceAdminServiceConfig` gains one **required** member, `listObjectsBoundTo(datasource)`: the objects that name the datasource, with their `external` binding. Required because it is the verdict's input; an optional seam would let a host store the very pair this closes.
- `DatasourceAdminServicePlugin` (`datasource-admin-plugin.ts`) answers it from the engine's object registry (the `objectql` service's `registry`), the registry the save door writes through to, so an object saved through `PUT /api/v1/meta/object/NAME` or imported from a remote table counts at once. Not the metadata service's `listObjects()`, which holds a boot-time copy that a runtime save never reaches (the reading `plugin.ts` records for the federation service).
- The existing `DatasourceAdminServiceConfig` fakes in this package's tests gain `listObjectsBoundTo: async () => []` (8 files, 10 fakes, no assertion moved).

## Contract

Every input whose answer changes, old to new:

1. **`POST /datasources`, `schemaMode: 'managed'` or none, and an object in the engine registry names that datasource with `external`.** Old: `201`, the record stored and registered, a supplied secret minted, the pool registered. New: `400 DATASOURCE_ADMIN_ERROR` naming each such object; nothing stored, registered or minted.
2. **`PATCH /datasources/NAME` that sets `schemaMode: 'managed'` on a federated datasource such objects bind.** Old: `200`, the row flipped, the pool rebuilt. New: the same `400`; the row, its secret and its pool untouched.
3. **`PATCH` of a judged key (or with a secret) on a datasource that is already managed and already bound `external`.** Old: `200`. New: the same `400`. The fix it names: declare the datasource `external` / `validate-only`, or remove `external` from the objects.

Unchanged: a federated datasource (`schemaMode: 'external'` or `'validate-only'`) and a datasource no object binds with `external` keep their answers (pinned on both doors); objects on the datasource with no `external` binding, and objects bound `external` to another datasource, are never in the verdict (pinned); a `label` / `active`-only `PATCH` is applied (pinned); `testConnection`, `removeDatasource` and `migrateCredential` are not touched (none of them changes `schemaMode`).

## Pins

- `src/__tests__/datasource-admin-external-binding.test.ts` (new, 11 cases): through the real routes over the real service. Each refusal asserts status, `error.code`, the predicate's own message per bound object (derived from `externalBindingDatasourceRefusal`, never restated) and the store after (no record, no secret, no `put` / `registerPool` / `reregisterPool` call). Controls: no `external` binding, federated `external` and `validate-only` on create, `validate-only` on update, managed with no external binding, label/active-only.
- `src/__tests__/datasource-admin-plugin.test.ts` (3 cases added): the plugin's seam reads the `objectql` registry while the metadata service's `listObjects()` is empty, so a runtime-saved object blocks create and the flip to managed; an object with no `external` binding does not.

**Ablation** (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, anchor `if (findings.length === 0) return undefined;` replaced by `return undefined;`, landed 1 to 0, restored to the HEAD blob `1c8772e150d7` with `git diff HEAD` empty): the two pin files went `7 failed | 35 passed`. The 7 red are exactly the refusal pins (5 door, 2 plugin); every control stayed green.

## Local verification

On `ab44e1bd`, over `origin/main` `f0fdd45bb`. Heavy runs went through the verify lock; each line cites its `VERDICT`.

- `pnpm exec turbo run build --filter='@objectstack/service-datasource^...'`: `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- `@objectstack/service-datasource` suite (`vitest run`): `VERDICT command-exit 0`; Test Files 56 passed (56); Tests 969 passed (969).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-datasource typecheck`: `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- `eslint --no-inline-config` on the changed `.ts` files: exit 0. `check-nul-bytes`: exit 0.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`: 68 families derived, each run, every one `exit 0` (`check:type-check-debt` under the lock; the build-reading families after the dogfood closure build).
- `--ran` reconciliation: `68 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 68 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero — all 68 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3)`.
- `check-adr-0087-registration --base origin/main` (in the derived set, on the committed head): exit 0 with the changeset's `not-required (already-registered object-external-binding-managed-datasource-refused)` disposition.
- The full dogfood battery is owed once on the final head (the `!` and the `(narrowing)` arm); its counts follow as a PR comment.

## Acceptance notes

- **The bound-object count behind `removeDatasource` reads the boot-time copy.** `countBoundObjects` / `countBoundObjectsDiagnosed` (`datasource-admin-plugin.ts:461`, `:486`) count from `metadata.listObjects()`, the copy `plugin.ts` records as taken once at boot and never reached by a runtime save. So an object imported or saved at runtime is not counted, and the removal guard can read `0` for a datasource such an object binds until the next restart. Read from code and from that recorded reading; not reproduced at the public door here, so not filed. This PR leaves the count alone (its own card's scope); the new seam reads the registry. Carrier: none.
- **Branch name.** This PR's branch is `claude/project-thread-29nfa9`, the name the session was given, not `claude/issue-25277-…`; the Duplicate Fix Guard may say so. The claim (comment 6365222748) names it.
